claim: In mouse, the pituitary gland undergoes active maturation immediately after birth.
source: In mouse, the gland undergoes active maturation immediately after birth.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about mouse pituitary development.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing revealed proliferative stem cell populations in the neonatal pituitary.
source: Single-cell RNA-sequencing pictured an active gland, revealing proliferative stem as well as hormonal (progenitor) cell populations.
evidence: This finding is directly stated in the abstract and supported by scRNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The neonatal pituitary stem cell pool displays a hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal phenotype.
source: The stem cell pool displayed a hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal phenotype, characteristic of development-involved tissue stem cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by gene expression data and immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal phenotype is characteristic of development-involved tissue stem cells.
source: The stem cell pool displayed a hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal phenotype, characteristic of development-involved tissue stem cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and further supported by citation to Dong et al., 2018 in the discussion.

claim: Organoid culturing recapitulates the neonatal pituitary stem cells' phenotype.
source: Organoid culturing recapitulated the stem cells' phenotype, interestingly also reproducing their paracrine activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through organoid culture experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Organoid culturing reproduces the paracrine activity of neonatal pituitary stem cells.
source: Organoid culturing recapitulated the stem cells' phenotype, interestingly also reproducing their paracrine activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by co-culture experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: IL-6 advances neonatal pituitary organoid growth.
source: The pituitary stem cell-activating interleukin-6 advanced organoid growth, although the neonatal stem cell compartment was not visibly affected in Il6−/− mice, likely due to cytokine family redundancy.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by organoid culture data shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: The neonatal stem cell compartment is not visibly affected in Il6−/− mice.
source: The pituitary stem cell-activating interleukin-6 advanced organoid growth, although the neonatal stem cell compartment was not visibly affected in Il6−/− mice, likely due to cytokine family redundancy.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Cytokine family redundancy likely explains the lack of visible effect on the neonatal stem cell compartment in Il6−/− mice.
source: The pituitary stem cell-activating interleukin-6 advanced organoid growth, although the neonatal stem cell compartment was not visibly affected in Il6−/− mice, likely due to cytokine family redundancy.
evidence: This is proposed as an explanation in the abstract and supported by data showing other cytokines can compensate (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C-E).

claim: The neonatal pituitary gland exhibits a pronounced WNT pathway.
source: Further transcriptomic analysis exposed a pronounced WNT pathway in the neonatal gland, shown to be involved in stem cell activation and to overlap with the (fetal) human pituitary transcriptome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by transcriptomic analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The WNT pathway is involved in neonatal pituitary stem cell activation.
source: Further transcriptomic analysis exposed a pronounced WNT pathway in the neonatal gland, shown to be involved in stem cell activation and to overlap with the (fetal) human pituitary transcriptome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by functional experiments with WNT inhibitors shown in Figure 3E-F.

claim: The WNT pathway in neonatal mouse pituitary overlaps with the fetal human pituitary transcriptome.
source: Further transcriptomic analysis exposed a pronounced WNT pathway in the neonatal gland, shown to be involved in stem cell activation and to overlap with the (fetal) human pituitary transcriptome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2G.

claim: The neonatal pituitary efficiently regenerates following local damage.
source: Following local damage, the neonatal gland efficiently regenerates, despite absence of additional stem cell proliferation, or upregulated IL-6 or WNT expression, all in line with the already high stem cell activation status, thereby exposing striking differences with adult pituitary.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by regeneration experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Following local damage, the neonatal pituitary does not show additional stem cell proliferation.
source: Following local damage, the neonatal gland efficiently regenerates, despite absence of additional stem cell proliferation, or upregulated IL-6 or WNT expression, all in line with the already high stem cell activation status, thereby exposing striking differences with adult pituitary.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Following local damage, the neonatal pituitary does not show upregulated IL-6 expression.
source: Following local damage, the neonatal gland efficiently regenerates, despite absence of additional stem cell proliferation, or upregulated IL-6 or WNT expression, all in line with the already high stem cell activation status, thereby exposing striking differences with adult pituitary.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Following local damage, the neonatal pituitary does not show upregulated WNT expression.
source: Following local damage, the neonatal gland efficiently regenerates, despite absence of additional stem cell proliferation, or upregulated IL-6 or WNT expression, all in line with the already high stem cell activation status, thereby exposing striking differences with adult pituitary.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The absence of additional stem cell activation following damage in neonatal pituitary is in line with the already high stem cell activation status.
source: Following local damage, the neonatal gland efficiently regenerates, despite absence of additional stem cell proliferation, or upregulated IL-6 or WNT expression, all in line with the already high stem cell activation status, thereby exposing striking differences with adult pituitary.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the abstract, connecting the observed lack of additional activation to the baseline activated state.

claim: There are striking differences between neonatal and adult pituitary in response to damage.
source: Following local damage, the neonatal gland efficiently regenerates, despite absence of additional stem cell proliferation, or upregulated IL-6 or WNT expression, all in line with the already high stem cell activation status, thereby exposing striking differences with adult pituitary.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by comparative data throughout the manuscript, particularly in the discussion referencing previous adult pituitary studies (Fu et al., 2012; Vennekens et al., 2021).

claim: The pituitary represents the endocrine master regulator.
source: As central hub of the endocrine system, the pituitary plays a quintessential role in governing the endocrine glands throughout the body, thereby regulating key physiological processes including growth, metabolism, fertility, stress, and immunity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about pituitary function.

claim: The pituitary regulates key physiological processes including growth, metabolism, fertility, stress, and immunity.
source: As central hub of the endocrine system, the pituitary plays a quintessential role in governing the endocrine glands throughout the body, thereby regulating key physiological processes including growth, metabolism, fertility, stress, and immunity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge, supported by citation to Melmed, 2011 and Willems and Vankelecom, 2014.

claim: The pituitary contains multiple endocrine cell types including somatotropes, corticotropes, lactotropes, gonadotropes, and thyrotropes.
source: To execute this primordial function, the pituitary has to properly develop into a compound gland of multiple endocrine cells, encompassing somatotropes (producing growth hormone [GH]), corticotropes (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]), lactotropes (prolactin [PRL]), gonadotropes (luteinizing hormone [LH] and/or follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH]), and thyrotropes (thyroid-stimulating hormone [TSH]) (Melmed, 2011; Willems and Vankelecom, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge, supported by citations to Melmed, 2011 and Willems and Vankelecom, 2014.

claim: Somatotropes produce growth hormone (GH).
source: To execute this primordial function, the pituitary has to properly develop into a compound gland of multiple endocrine cells, encompassing somatotropes (producing growth hormone [GH]), corticotropes (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]), lactotropes (prolactin [PRL]), gonadotropes (luteinizing hormone [LH] and/or follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH]), and thyrotropes (thyroid-stimulating hormone [TSH]) (Melmed, 2011; Willems and Vankelecom, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Corticotropes produce adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH).
source: To execute this primordial function, the pituitary has to properly develop into a compound gland of multiple endocrine cells, encompassing somatotropes (producing growth hormone [GH]), corticotropes (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]), lactotropes (prolactin [PRL]), gonadotropes (luteinizing hormone [LH] and/or follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH]), and thyrotropes (thyroid-stimulating hormone [TSH]) (Melmed, 2011; Willems and Vankelecom, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Lactotropes produce prolactin (PRL).
source: To execute this primordial function, the pituitary has to properly develop into a compound gland of multiple endocrine cells, encompassing somatotropes (producing growth hormone [GH]), corticotropes (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]), lactotropes (prolactin [PRL]), gonadotropes (luteinizing hormone [LH] and/or follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH]), and thyrotropes (thyroid-stimulating hormone [TSH]) (Melmed, 2011; Willems and Vankelecom, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Gonadotropes produce luteinizing hormone (LH) and/or follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
source: To execute this primordial function, the pituitary has to properly develop into a compound gland of multiple endocrine cells, encompassing somatotropes (producing growth hormone [GH]), corticotropes (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]), lactotropes (prolactin [PRL]), gonadotropes (luteinizing hormone [LH] and/or follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH]), and thyrotropes (thyroid-stimulating hormone [TSH]) (Melmed, 2011; Willems and Vankelecom, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Thyrotropes produce thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).
source: To execute this primordial function, the pituitary has to properly develop into a compound gland of multiple endocrine cells, encompassing somatotropes (producing growth hormone [GH]), corticotropes (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]), lactotropes (prolactin [PRL]), gonadotropes (luteinizing hormone [LH] and/or follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH]), and thyrotropes (thyroid-stimulating hormone [TSH]) (Melmed, 2011; Willems and Vankelecom, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The mouse pituitary undergoes intense growth and maturation during the first postnatal weeks.
source: In the mouse, the pituitary undergoes an intense growth and maturation process during the first postnatal weeks, with number and size of hormone-producing cells substantively expanding following proliferation of committed (progenitor) and endocrine cells (Carbajo-Pérez and Watanabe, 1990; Laporte et al., 2021; Sasaki, 1988; Taniguchi et al., 2002; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: During the first postnatal weeks, the number and size of hormone-producing cells in mouse pituitary expand following proliferation of committed progenitor and endocrine cells.
source: In the mouse, the pituitary undergoes an intense growth and maturation process during the first postnatal weeks, with number and size of hormone-producing cells substantively expanding following proliferation of committed (progenitor) and endocrine cells (Carbajo-Pérez and Watanabe, 1990; Laporte et al., 2021; Sasaki, 1988; Taniguchi et al., 2002; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The neonatal pituitary stem cell compartment shows elevated abundance compared to adult pituitary.
source: Simultaneously, the local stem cell (SOX2+) compartment shows signs of activation including elevated abundance and expression of stemness pathways when compared to the adult pituitary stem cells (Gremeaux et al., 2012; Laporte et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to Gremeaux et al., 2012 and Laporte et al., 2021.

claim: The neonatal pituitary stem cell compartment shows elevated expression of stemness pathways compared to adult pituitary.
source: Simultaneously, the local stem cell (SOX2+) compartment shows signs of activation including elevated abundance and expression of stemness pathways when compared to the adult pituitary stem cells (Gremeaux et al., 2012; Laporte et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Pituitary stem cells can give rise to new endocrine cells.
source: The stem cells can give rise to new endocrine cells, a property which has been found most prominent (although not extensive) during this neonatal period (Andoniadou et al., 2013; Rizzoti et al., 2013; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The ability of pituitary stem cells to give rise to new endocrine cells is most prominent during the neonatal period.
source: The stem cells can give rise to new endocrine cells, a property which has been found most prominent (although not extensive) during this neonatal period (Andoniadou et al., 2013; Rizzoti et al., 2013; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Stem cells in the mature, adult pituitary are quiescent.
source: In contrast, stem cells in the mature, adult pituitary are quiescent and do not highly contribute to new endocrine cells during the (slow) homeostatic turnover of the gland (Andoniadou et al., 2013; Laporte et al., 2021; Rizzoti et al., 2013; Vankelecom and Chen, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Adult pituitary stem cells do not highly contribute to new endocrine cells during homeostatic turnover.
source: In contrast, stem cells in the mature, adult pituitary are quiescent and do not highly contribute to new endocrine cells during the (slow) homeostatic turnover of the gland (Andoniadou et al., 2013; Laporte et al., 2021; Rizzoti et al., 2013; Vankelecom and Chen, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Adult pituitary stem cells become activated following local injury in the gland.
source: However, the adult stem cells become activated following local injury in the gland, showing a proliferative reaction and signs of differentiation toward the ablated cells, coinciding with substantial regeneration (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Fu et al., 2012.

claim: Following local injury, adult pituitary stem cells show a proliferative reaction and signs of differentiation toward the ablated cells.
source: However, the adult stem cells become activated following local injury in the gland, showing a proliferative reaction and signs of differentiation toward the ablated cells, coinciding with substantial regeneration (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: IL-6 is upregulated in adult pituitary stem cells upon local damage.
source: We recently identified interleukin-6 (IL-6) to be upregulated in the adult pituitary (in particular its stem cells) upon this local damage which activated the stem cells (Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Vennekens et al., 2021.

claim: IL-6 activates adult pituitary stem cells upon local damage.
source: We recently identified interleukin-6 (IL-6) to be upregulated in the adult pituitary (in particular its stem cells) upon this local damage which activated the stem cells (Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: After quality control, 21,419 good-quality single cells from neonatal AP were retained for analysis.
source: First, low-quality/dead cells and potential doublets (i.e., with less than 750 genes or more than 8000 genes and more than 17.5% mitochondrial RNA; see cutoffs in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) were removed, resulting in a total of 21,419 good-quality single cells (i.e., 9618 from undamaged AP and 11,801 from damaged AP) for downstream analyses.
evidence: This is stated in the scRNA-seq analysis methods section describing the quality control process.

claim: The neonatal AP contains 9,618 good-quality single cells from undamaged samples.
source: First, low-quality/dead cells and potential doublets (i.e., with less than 750 genes or more than 8000 genes and more than 17.5% mitochondrial RNA; see cutoffs in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) were removed, resulting in a total of 21,419 good-quality single cells (i.e., 9618 from undamaged AP and 11,801 from damaged AP) for downstream analyses.
evidence: This is stated in the scRNA-seq analysis methods section.

claim: The neonatal AP contains 11,801 good-quality single cells from damaged samples.
source: First, low-quality/dead cells and potential doublets (i.e., with less than 750 genes or more than 8000 genes and more than 17.5% mitochondrial RNA; see cutoffs in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) were removed, resulting in a total of 21,419 good-quality single cells (i.e., 9618 from undamaged AP and 11,801 from damaged AP) for downstream analyses.
evidence: This is stated in the scRNA-seq analysis methods section.

claim: Two stem cell subclusters (SC1 and SC2) are present in the neonatal AP.
source: In particular, two stem cell subclusters (SC1 and SC2) were discerned in the neonatal AP as before also identified in the adult gland (Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SC1 displays more prominent expression of keratins Krt8 and Krt18 compared to SC2.
source: These subclusters exhibit a diverging transcriptomic fingerprint, with SC1 displaying more prominent expression of keratins Krt8 and Krt18, and SC2 of Six1 and Sox2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), similar to the adult gland (Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: SC2 displays more prominent expression of Six1 and Sox2 compared to SC1.
source: These subclusters exhibit a diverging transcriptomic fingerprint, with SC1 displaying more prominent expression of keratins Krt8 and Krt18, and SC2 of Six1 and Sox2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), similar to the adult gland (Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The stem cell populations (SC1 and SC2) are three- to fourfold larger in neonatal than adult AP.
source: First, the stem cell populations (both SC1 and SC2) are larger in neonatal than adult AP (three- to fourfold; Figure 1A), corroborated in situ by immunofluorescence analysis of the SOX2+ cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The neonatal SOX2+ cell compartment shows higher proliferative activity than adult.
source: Moreover, higher proliferative activity was observed in this SOX2+ cell compartment (as assessed by Ki67 immunoanalysis; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), as also found before (Gremeaux et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and citation to Gremeaux et al., 2012.

claim: A proliferative stem cell cluster (Prolif SC) is present in the neonatal AP but not in the adult gland.
source: In accordance, the scRNA-seq interrogation exposed a clear proliferative stem cell cluster (Prolif SC; as identified by coexpression of proliferation genes Mki67, Pcna, Top2a, Mcm6, with stem cell markers Sox2, Krt8, Sox9) in the neonatal AP, not discerned in the adult gland (Figure 1A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A, B.

claim: The Prolif SC cluster is identified by coexpression of proliferation genes (Mki67, Pcna, Top2a, Mcm6) with stem cell markers (Sox2, Krt8, Sox9).
source: In accordance, the scRNA-seq interrogation exposed a clear proliferative stem cell cluster (Prolif SC; as identified by coexpression of proliferation genes Mki67, Pcna, Top2a, Mcm6, with stem cell markers Sox2, Krt8, Sox9) in the neonatal AP, not discerned in the adult gland (Figure 1A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the identification of the Prolif SC cluster.

claim: Proliferative Pou1f1+ cell clusters are present exclusively in the neonatal gland.
source: Interestingly, proliferative subclusters were also perceived for other cell types, moreover exclusively in the neonatal gland. First, we discerned a proliferative Pou1f1+ (Pit1+) cell group.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A proliferative corticotrope subcluster is present exclusively in the neonatal gland.
source: In addition, we distinguished a proliferative corticotrope subcluster.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The neonatal AP contains gonadotrope progenitor and precursor subclusters.
source: Strikingly, the neonatal AP also contains gonadotrope progenitor and precursor subclusters as characterized by gradually increasing gonadotrope markers (Nr5a1, Cga, Lhb, Fshb, and Gnrhr) in parallel with declining stem cell factors (Sox2, Krt8, and Sox9) (Figure 1A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A, B.

claim: Gonadotrope progenitor and precursor subclusters are characterized by gradually increasing gonadotrope markers (Nr5a1, Cga, Lhb, Fshb, and Gnrhr) in parallel with declining stem cell factors (Sox2, Krt8, and Sox9).
source: Strikingly, the neonatal AP also contains gonadotrope progenitor and precursor subclusters as characterized by gradually increasing gonadotrope markers (Nr5a1, Cga, Lhb, Fshb, and Gnrhr) in parallel with declining stem cell factors (Sox2, Krt8, and Sox9) (Figure 1A, B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the gonadotrope progenitor/precursor subclusters.

claim: The gonadotrope lineage arises last during embryonic development just before birth.
source: The gonadotrope lineage arises last during embryonic development just before birth (Stallings et al., 2016), and some cells in the neonatal AP indeed coexpress SOX2 and the common gonadotropin subunit αGSU (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citation to Stallings et al., 2016.

claim: Some cells in the neonatal AP coexpress SOX2 and αGSU.
source: The gonadotrope lineage arises last during embryonic development just before birth (Stallings et al., 2016), and some cells in the neonatal AP indeed coexpress SOX2 and the common gonadotropin subunit αGSU (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Hormonal cell types (particularly somatotropes and lactotropes) rise in abundance toward adulthood.
source: While the hormonal cell types (particularly somatotropes and lactotropes) rise in abundance toward adulthood, stem cells as well as supportive mesenchymal cells (MC) are more numerous in the neonatal gland (Figure 1A), suggesting that the latter populations play an active role in the critical development and growth of the gland at this acute period after birth, which becomes less prominent at mature age.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Stem cells and supportive mesenchymal cells are more numerous in the neonatal gland than in adult.
source: While the hormonal cell types (particularly somatotropes and lactotropes) rise in abundance toward adulthood, stem cells as well as supportive mesenchymal cells (MC) are more numerous in the neonatal gland (Figure 1A), suggesting that the latter populations play an active role in the critical development and growth of the gland at this acute period after birth, which becomes less prominent at mature age.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Stem cells and mesenchymal cells play an active role in the critical development and growth of the neonatal gland.
source: While the hormonal cell types (particularly somatotropes and lactotropes) rise in abundance toward adulthood, stem cells as well as supportive mesenchymal cells (MC) are more numerous in the neonatal gland (Figure 1A), suggesting that the latter populations play an active role in the critical development and growth of the gland at this acute period after birth, which becomes less prominent at mature age.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion in the results section based on the observed cell abundance patterns.

claim: The stem cell compartment of neonatal AP displays a highly mixed epithelial/mesenchymal phenotype that is clearly faded in the adult gland.
source: Surprisingly, the stem cell compartment of the neonatal AP displays a highly mixed epithelial/mesenchymal (E/M) phenotype, manifestly expressing both epithelial and mesenchymal markers, which is clearly faded in the adult gland (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cells that coexpress CK8/18 and vimentin are found in the marginal zone SOX2+ stem cell niche of the neonatal pituitary.
source: In accordance, cells that coexpress the epithelial markers cytokeratin 8 and 18 (CK8/18) and the mesenchymal marker vimentin (VIM) were found in the marginal zone (MZ) SOX2+ stem cell niche of the neonatal pituitary, and were visibly less prominent in the adult gland (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Coexpression of SOX2 with VIM is more pronounced in the neonatal gland than adult.
source: Similarly, coexpression of SOX2 with VIM was more pronounced in the neonatal gland (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A hybrid E/M character is present in stem/progenitor cells of developing organs such as lung, intestine, and liver.
source: More in general, a hybrid E/M nature is present in stem/progenitor cells of developing organs (such as lung, intestine, and liver), and underlies their active contribution to the tissues' development (Dong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Dong et al., 2018.

claim: A hybrid E/M phenotype underlies the active contribution of stem/progenitor cells to tissue development.
source: More in general, a hybrid E/M nature is present in stem/progenitor cells of developing organs (such as lung, intestine, and liver), and underlies their active contribution to the tissues' development (Dong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: A hybrid E/M phenotype was found in the stem/progenitor cell cluster of the fetal human pituitary.
source: Recently, a hybrid E/M phenotype was also uncovered in the stem/progenitor cell cluster of the fetal human pituitary, with the mesenchymal aspect lowering along further maturation (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2020.

claim: The mesenchymal aspect of the hybrid E/M phenotype lowers along further maturation in fetal human pituitary.
source: Recently, a hybrid E/M phenotype was also uncovered in the stem/progenitor cell cluster of the fetal human pituitary, with the mesenchymal aspect lowering along further maturation (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition plays a role in mouse pituitary development through driving the exit of stem cells from the MZ toward the developing AP.
source: Moreover, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition has been reported to play a role in mouse pituitary development through driving the exit of stem cells from the MZ toward the developing AP (Pérez Millán et al., 2016; Yoshida et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Pérez Millán et al., 2016 and Yoshida et al., 2016.

claim: Organoids developing from adult mouse AP originate from the SOX2+ stem cells.
source: We have shown that organoids developing from adult mouse AP originate from the SOX2+ stem cells and reflect their phenotype and activation state (e.g., higher organoid number following damage [Cox et al., 2019; Vennekens et al., 2021]), thus serving as a valuable pituitary stem cell biology research model and activation readout tool (Cox et al., 2019; Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to Cox et al., 2019 and Vennekens et al., 2021.

claim: Organoids reflect the phenotype and activation state of pituitary stem cells.
source: We have shown that organoids developing from adult mouse AP originate from the SOX2+ stem cells and reflect their phenotype and activation state (e.g., higher organoid number following damage [Cox et al., 2019; Vennekens et al., 2021]), thus serving as a valuable pituitary stem cell biology research model and activation readout tool (Cox et al., 2019; Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations.

claim: Individual removal of FGF2/8/10, nicotinamide, SHH, A83-01, noggin and IGF-1 from PitOM resulted in increased organoid number from neonatal AP.
source: Surprisingly, individual removal of several growth and signaling factors (i.e., fibroblast growth factors [FGF] 2/8/10, nicotinamide, sonic hedgehog [SHH], the transforming growth factor-β [TGFβ] inhibitor A83-01, the bone morphogenetic protein [BMP] inhibitor noggin and insulin-like growth factor 1 [IGF-1]) from the adult AP-geared PitOM resulted in a visible increase in organoid number developing from neonatal AP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), indicating that these PitOM-included factors are not essential (rather impedimental) for organoid outgrowth from the neonatal gland.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Neonatal pituitary stem cells show high expression of Fgf10, Igf1, their receptors Fgfr2 and Igf1r, and noggin compared to adult stem cells.
source: Indeed, the neonatal pituitary stem cells show high expression of several of these factors, suggesting already prominent intrinsic pathway activity. Among others, Fgf10 and Igf1, together with their receptors Fgfr2 and Igf1r, and noggin (Nog) are found upregulated in the neonatal stem cell compartment (SC1+SC2+Prolif SC) as compared to the adult stem cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The expression pattern of Fgf10, Igf1, Fgfr2, Igf1r, and Nog is retained in neonatal pituitary-derived organoids.
source: Moreover, this expression pattern is retained in the neonatal pituitary-derived organoids (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CT, p38i, RSPO1 and EGF are essential for neonatal AP organoid formation.
source: In contrast, cholera toxin (CT), p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) inhibitor (p38i; SB202190), the WNT-signaling amplifier R-spondin 1 (RSPO1) and epithelial growth factor (EGF) were found essential since organoid formation was largely abrogated in the absence of each one of these factors (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The number of organoids that developed from neonatal AP in RSpECT medium is significantly higher than from adult gland.
source: Using the optimized RSpECT medium, the number of organoids that developed from neonatal AP was significantly higher than from adult gland (for which RSpECT did not change the formed organoid number) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The proportion of organoid-initiating SOX2+ cells is ~10-fold higher in neonatal than adult AP.
source: Of note, the much larger number (~40-fold) can only partially be explained by the higher abundance of SOX2+ cells in the neonatal AP (~3- to 4-fold; see above). Indeed, normalized to the absolute number of SOX2+ cells seeded per well, the proportion of organoid-initiating SOX2+ cells is ~10-fold higher in neonatal than adult AP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Organoid formation efficiency reflects the higher intrinsic activation status of neonatal pituitary stem cells.
source: Thus, organoid formation efficiency reflects the higher intrinsic activation (or 'primed') status of neonatal pituitary stem cells per se.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the results section based on the organoid formation data.

claim: Seeding AP from neonatal Sox2eGFP/+ reporter mice generated only eGFP+ organoids.
source: The organoids, as before shown for adult AP (Cox et al., 2019), originated from the tissue-resident SOX2+ stem cells. Seeding AP from neonatal Sox2eGFP/+ reporter mice (expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein [eGFP] in SOX2+ cells) generated only organoids that were fluorescent (eGFP+; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: When Sox2eGFP/+ AP cells were mixed with wildtype cells, organoids that developed were either eGFP+ or not, pointing to a clonal origin.
source: Furthermore, when Sox2eGFP/+ AP cells were mixed with wildtype (WT) cells, organoids that developed were either eGFP+ or not (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), thereby pointing to a clonal origin, as further supported by live-culture time-lapse imaging showing organoids growing from individual cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Neonatal AP organoids express SOX2, E-cadherin, CK8/18, and TACSTD2.
source: The obtained organoids display a pituitary stemness phenotype expressing SOX2 as well as other known pituitary stem cell markers (such as E-cadherin, CK8/18, TACSTD2 (alias TROP2) [Chen et al., 2009; Cox et al., 2019; Fauquier et al., 2008; Vennekens et al., 2021]) (Figure 2C, Videos 2 and 3), while being devoid of hormone expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2C and Videos 2 and 3.

claim: Neonatal AP organoids are devoid of hormone expression.
source: The obtained organoids display a pituitary stemness phenotype expressing SOX2 as well as other known pituitary stem cell markers (such as E-cadherin, CK8/18, TACSTD2 (alias TROP2) [Chen et al., 2009; Cox et al., 2019; Fauquier et al., 2008; Vennekens et al., 2021]) (Figure 2C, Videos 2 and 3), while being devoid of hormone expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Stem cells in early-postnatal (PD14) pituitary can function as autocrine and paracrine signaling center.
source: Very recently, it has been reported that stem cells in early-postnatal (PD14) pituitary can function as autocrine and paracrine signaling center, among others stimulating proliferation within the own stem cell compartment (Russell et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citation to Russell et al., 2021.

claim: Neonatal (PD7) AP organoids elevate the outgrowth of organoids from adult AP when co-cultured.
source: Interestingly, when co-cultured, neonatal (PD7) AP organoids (as developed from WT mice) elevate the outgrowth of organoids from adult AP (as established from ubiquitously tdTomato(tdT)-expressing ROSA26mT/mG mice) (Figure 2D), coinciding with increased proliferation of the adult AP organoid-constituting stem cells, showing a Ki67+ index reaching the one of neonatal AP-derived organoids (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Co-culture with neonatal AP organoids increases proliferation of adult AP organoid-constituting stem cells.
source: Interestingly, when co-cultured, neonatal (PD7) AP organoids (as developed from WT mice) elevate the outgrowth of organoids from adult AP (as established from ubiquitously tdTomato(tdT)-expressing ROSA26mT/mG mice) (Figure 2D), coinciding with increased proliferation of the adult AP organoid-constituting stem cells, showing a Ki67+ index reaching the one of neonatal AP-derived organoids (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Il6 gene expression is low in neonatal AP when compared to adult gland.
source: Intriguingly, gene expression of Il6 is low in neonatal AP when compared to adult gland (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Stat3 regulon activity is low in neonatal AP compared to adult gland.
source: Similarly, gene-regulatory network (regulon) activity of the IL-6 signal-mediating JAK/STAT member Stat3 is low as compared to adult gland (analysis using 'single-cell regulatory network inference' (SCENIC) [Aibar et al., 2017]) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A significantly smaller number of organoids grew from Il6−/− versus WT neonatal AP.
source: Indeed, a significantly smaller number of organoids grew from Il6 knockout (Il6−/−) versus WT neonatal AP, which was (partially) rescued by adding exogenous IL-6 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Adding exogenous IL-6 partially rescues organoid formation from Il6−/− neonatal AP.
source: Indeed, a significantly smaller number of organoids grew from Il6 knockout (Il6−/−) versus WT neonatal AP, which was (partially) rescued by adding exogenous IL-6 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: IL-6 addition strongly enhanced the passageability of neonatal AP organoid cultures from 4-5 passages without IL-6 to at least 15 passages with the cytokine.
source: Moreover, although IL-6 addition did not significantly increase the number of organoids formed from WT (Il6+/+) neonatal AP (most likely because the stem cell activation status is already high) (Figure 2E), it strongly enhanced the passageability of the organoid cultures, from 4 to 5 passages without IL-6 to at least 15 passages (6 months of expansive culture) with the cytokine (Figure 2F), as also observed before for adult AP (Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Endogenous IL-6 levels decline at organoid passaging.
source: Addition of IL-6 is considered to compensate for the decline in endogenous levels that is observed at passaging (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Neonatal AP organoids robustly retain their stemness phenotype during long-term expansion.
source: Of note, the organoids robustly retained their stemness phenotype during the long-term expansion, showing consistent stem cell marker expression (and hormone absence) between early (P2) and late (P8–11) passage (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Expression of Il11, Lif, and Tnf is slightly enhanced in the neonatal Il6−/− AP.
source: Expression of the IL-6 family members Il11 and leukemia-inhibitory factor (Lif), and of the related cytokine tumor necrosis factor-α (Tnf), was found slightly enhanced in the neonatal Il6−/− AP (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: LIF and IL-11 enhanced organoid expandability similar to IL-6.
source: These cytokines, as well as the related IL-1β, did not significantly increase the number of organoids formed, but enhanced organoid expandability (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D), all similar to IL-6 (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3D.

claim: The effects of TNFα and IL-1β on organoid formation are mediated by IL-6.
source: The effects of TNFα and IL-1β seem to be mediated by IL-6 since these cytokines did not rescue its absence in organoid culturing from Il6−/− AP (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E), and increased the expression of IL-6 (as measured in WT AP organoids) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3E-F.

claim: LIF and IL-11 can substitute for IL-6 in organoid formation from Il6−/− AP.
source: In contrast, the IL-6 family members LIF and IL-11, known to act through the same gp130/JAK–STAT pathway (Rose-John, 2018), could substitute for IL-6 since increasing the number of developing organoids from Il6−/− AP as well as their expansion (passaging), while not affecting Il6 expression in WT AP organoids (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3E-F.

claim: LIF and IL-11 act through the same gp130/JAK–STAT pathway.
source: In contrast, the IL-6 family members LIF and IL-11, known to act through the same gp130/JAK–STAT pathway (Rose-John, 2018), could substitute for IL-6 since increasing the number of developing organoids from Il6−/− AP as well as their expansion (passaging), while not affecting Il6 expression in WT AP organoids (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citation to Rose-John, 2018.

claim: Adding STAT3 inhibitor STATTIC strongly reduces organoid development and expansion.
source: An important underlying role of JAK–STAT signaling in organoid development as well as expansion is supported by the strong reduction of both processes when adding the STAT3 inhibitor STATTIC (Figure 2—figure supplement 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3G.

claim: Multiple WNT signaling-associated genes are significantly increased in neonatal versus adult stem cell clusters.
source: DEG analysis revealed significantly increased expression of multiple WNT signaling-associated genes (e.g., Frizzled (Fzd)2, Fzd3, Gsk3b, Ctnnb1, and Tnks) in the neonatal versus adult stem cell clusters (Figure 3A; Figure 3—source data 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Biological WNT pathway terms are enriched in the neonatal stem cell compartment.
source: In analogy, GO analysis exposed that biological WNT pathway terms are enriched in the neonatal stem cell compartment (Figure 3B; Figure 3—source data 1B), and GSEA examination showed significant enrichment of WNT-associated hallmarks (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Regulon activity of Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 is most prominent in the stem cell clusters compared to endocrine cell clusters.
source: Regulon activity of the WNT downstream transcription factors Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 is most prominent in the stem cell clusters (SC1, SC2, and Prolif SC) when compared to the endocrine cell clusters (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Regulon activity of Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 is higher in neonatal than adult gland.
source: Clearly, regulon activity of these WNT transcription factors is higher in neonatal than adult gland (Figure 3C, violin plots).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: WNT ligands and receptors are overall higher expressed in neonatal than adult AP.
source: Furthermore, looking at upstream WNT pathway components, we found that ligands and receptors are overall higher expressed at neonatal age as analyzed in the whole AP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Wnt5a and Fzd2 receptor are much higher expressed in neonatal stem cell and MC clusters compared to adult.
source: Regarding the stem cell and MC clusters, particularly Wnt5a and Fzd2 receptor are much higher expressed (both virtually absent in the adult AP) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The WNT pathway is proposed to contribute to the activated state of the neonatal stem cell compartment.
source: Taken together, the WNT pathway is more prominently present in the neonatal gland, which is proposed to contribute to the activated state of the stem cell compartment.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the results section based on the WNT pathway expression data.

claim: A pronounced WNT profile has been reported in the PD14 mouse pituitary.
source: A pronounced WNT profile has recently also been reported in the later PD14 mouse pituitary (Russell et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citation to Russell et al., 2021.

claim: CellPhoneDB projects multiple reciprocal interactions of Wnt5a with canonical (Fzd) and noncanonical (Ror1) receptors between MC and stem cells.
source: Multiple reciprocal interactions of Wnt5a with canonical (Fzd) and noncanonical (Ror1) receptors are projected (Figure 3D), with Fzd1, Fzd3, and Fzd6 being the prevalent mediating receptors in the stem cells, and Fzd2 both in the stem cells and MC (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Rspo3, predominantly expressed by MC cells, is forecasted to mainly bind to Lgr4 and Lgr6 receptors on the stem cells.
source: Within the RSPO/LGR-driven WNT amplification system, Rspo3, being predominantly expressed by MC cells, is forecasted to mainly bind to Lgr4 and Lgr6 receptors on the stem cells (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: RNAscope confirmed the pronounced expression of Lgr4 and Lgr6 in the Sox2+ stem cells in situ.
source: RNAscope confirmed the pronounced expression of Lgr4 and Lgr6 in the Sox2+ stem cells in situ, clearly different from Rspo3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Addition of XAV-939 at seeding completely abolished neonatal AP organoid formation.
source: Addition of the WNT inhibitor XAV-939 (XAV; stabilizing the WNT-inhibitory protein AXIN2) at seeding (passage 0 [P0]) completely abolished organoid formation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Addition of IWP2 to seeded neonatal AP cells significantly reduced the number of organoids formed.
source: Addition of IWP2 (which blocks endogenous WNT ligand palmitoylation, as needed for secretion from the cell) to the seeded AP cells significantly reduced the number of organoids formed, which was substantially rescued by adding exogenous WNT5A and WNT3A (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Adding exogenous WNT5A and WNT3A substantially rescued organoid formation reduced by IWP2.
source: Addition of IWP2 (which blocks endogenous WNT ligand palmitoylation, as needed for secretion from the cell) to the seeded AP cells significantly reduced the number of organoids formed, which was substantially rescued by adding exogenous WNT5A and WNT3A (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Both XAV-939 and IWP2 decreased the proliferative activity in neonatal AP organoids.
source: Of note, both WNT inhibitors decreased the proliferative activity in the organoids (added to formed organoids at d7 of P0; Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Neonatal AP organoid growth is dependent on endogenous WNT activity.
source: Together, these findings show that neonatal AP organoid growth, which reflects stem cell biology/activation, is dependent on (endogenous) WNT activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on the WNT inhibitor experiments.

claim: RSPO1 is only slightly expressed in the neonatal pituitary.
source: Notably, RSPO1, which is typically used in organoid culturing (as we also did here and before, see Appendix 1—table 1; Cox et al., 2019; Vennekens et al., 2021), is only slightly expressed in the neonatal pituitary (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D) whereas Rspo3 expression is prominent (especially in the MC cluster; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: RSPO3 is capable of replacing RSPO1 for efficient neonatal AP organoid formation.
source: This naturally abundant RSPO ligand was found capable to replace RSPO1 for efficient organoid formation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Addition of WNT5A or WNT3A to adult AP cultures increased stem cell proliferation in the organoids resulting in larger organoid structures.
source: In support, addition of WNT5A or WNT3A to cultures from adult AP in which the stem cells are basically not activated (quiescent) (Vennekens et al., 2021) and the WNT pathway is much less prominent (Figure 3A–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B), increased stem cell proliferation in the organoids resulting in larger organoid structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Adding DKK1 to co-culture of neonatal and adult AP organoids resulted in decreased proliferative activity in the adult organoids.
source: Moreover, adding the WNT-signaling inhibitor Dickkopf 1 (DKK1) (which binds to the WNT co-receptors LRP5/6 thereby blocking WNT ligand action) to the co-culture of neonatal (WT) and adult (tdT+) AP organoids resulted in decreased proliferative activity in the adult organoids (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F), strongly supporting that the proliferation-activating effect of the neonatal organoid (stem) cells on the adult organoid (stem) cells, when cultured together (see Figure 2D), is mediated, at least partly, by paracrine WNT activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F.

claim: The proliferation-activating effect of neonatal organoid stem cells on adult organoid stem cells is mediated, at least partly, by paracrine WNT activity.
source: Moreover, adding the WNT-signaling inhibitor Dickkopf 1 (DKK1) (which binds to the WNT co-receptors LRP5/6 thereby blocking WNT ligand action) to the co-culture of neonatal (WT) and adult (tdT+) AP organoids resulted in decreased proliferative activity in the adult organoids (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F), strongly supporting that the proliferation-activating effect of the neonatal organoid (stem) cells on the adult organoid (stem) cells, when cultured together (see Figure 2D), is mediated, at least partly, by paracrine WNT activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on the DKK1 experiment.

claim: Treatment with LGK-974 decreased WNT target gene (Axin2 and Lgr5) expression in neonatal AP.
source: WNT target gene (Axin2 and Lgr5) expression in the AP diminished following LGK administration, thereby verifying its activity and efficacy at the level of the pituitary (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Treatment with LGK-974 decreased the number of proliferating SOX2+ cells in neonatal AP.
source: Interestingly, the number of proliferating SOX2+ cells decreased (Figure 3F), thus further supporting the involvement of WNT signaling in the activated phenotype of the neonatal AP stem cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The neonatal mouse and fetal human pituitary show significant overlap and high concordance in clustering outcome.
source: First, we found that the mouse neonatal and fetal human pituitary showed significant overlap and high concordance in clustering outcome (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G.

claim: In utero development of humans is more extended than of mice.
source: Of note, in utero development of humans is more extended than of mice (Xue et al., 2013), and the neonatal mouse stage thus rather corresponds to (late) embryonic stage in humans.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citation to Xue et al., 2013.

claim: The neonatal mouse stage corresponds to late embryonic stage in humans.
source: Of note, in utero development of humans is more extended than of mice (Xue et al., 2013), and the neonatal mouse stage thus rather corresponds to (late) embryonic stage in humans.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the developmental timing difference.

claim: WNT-associated genes show comparable expression pattern in fetal human pituitary as in neonatal mouse AP.
source: Projection of above specified WNT-associated genes on the human fetal pituitary UMAP plot revealed a comparable expression pattern as in neonatal mouse AP, with, for instance, WNT5A being expressed in the SC and MC clusters, and RSPO3 being most pronounced in the MC cluster (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3G.

claim: IL6 is expressed in the human fetal pituitary stem cells at similarly low levels as in the neonatal mouse pituitary.
source: Of note, IL6 is also expressed in the human fetal pituitary stem cells, moreover at similarly low levels as in the neonatal mouse pituitary (Figure 3—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2H.

claim: Three-day DT injection of neonatal GHCre/iDTR pups resulted in 50-60% ablation of GH+ cells.
source: Three-day diphtheria toxin (DT) injection of neonatal (PD4) GhCre/+;ROSA26iDTR/+ pups (further referred to as GHCre/iDTR mice, or 'damaged' condition) (Figure 4A) resulted in 50–60% ablation of GH+ cells (Figure 4B) (as compared to 80–90% ablation at adult age [Fu et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: DT-induced damage results in 80-90% somatotrope ablation in adult pituitary.
source: Three-day diphtheria toxin (DT) injection of neonatal (PD4) GhCre/+;ROSA26iDTR/+ pups (further referred to as GHCre/iDTR mice, or 'damaged' condition) (Figure 4A) resulted in 50–60% ablation of GH+ cells (Figure 4B) (as compared to 80–90% ablation at adult age [Fu et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citation to Fu et al., 2012.

claim: The neonatal stem cell compartment did not visibly react to damage (no increase in SOX2+ cells and their proliferative index).
source: The stem cell compartment did not visibly react (i.e., no increase in SOX2+ cells and their proliferative index, neither proportion-wise nor in absolute cell numbers; Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), which may be due to their already high activation status.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The lack of stem cell reaction to damage in neonatal pituitary may be due to their already high activation status.
source: The stem cell compartment did not visibly react (i.e., no increase in SOX2+ cells and their proliferative index, neither proportion-wise nor in absolute cell numbers; Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), which may be due to their already high activation status.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation in the results section.

claim: The somatotrope cell population was fully restored to normal numbers after 2 months in damaged neonatal pituitary.
source: Fascinatingly, the somatotrope cell population was fully restored to normal numbers, moreover already achieved after 2 months (Figure 4D), meaning a more efficient regenerative capacity of the dynamic neonatal AP than the adult gland (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The neonatal AP has a more efficient regenerative capacity than the adult gland.
source: Fascinatingly, the somatotrope cell population was fully restored to normal numbers, moreover already achieved after 2 months (Figure 4D), meaning a more efficient regenerative capacity of the dynamic neonatal AP than the adult gland (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by comparison to adult regeneration data from Fu et al., 2012.

claim: Il6 expression was not upregulated in the neonatal stem cell and MC clusters following damage.
source: First, in strong contrast to our recent findings in adult pituitary (Vennekens et al., 2021), Il6 expression, being very low in neonatal pituitary (see above), was not upregulated in the stem cell and MC clusters following damage (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), in line with a lack of extra stem cell activation (while IL-6 activates the stem cells in adult pituitary following damage [Vennekens et al., 2021]), together indicating that there is a striking difference in adult and neonatal pituitary (stem cell) reaction to damage.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The WNT pathway did not become extra activated following damage in neonatal pituitary.
source: Moreover, also in line with the absence of additional stem cell activation, the WNT pathway appeared not to become extra fired, neither immediately upon damage (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), nor at later timepoints during the regenerative period (i.e., one (PD14) and two (PD21) weeks after damage infliction), as assessed by Lgr5 and Axin2 target gene expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: A cluster of Pou1f1 lineage progenitors became distinguishable in the aggregate neonatal AP analysis (control + damaged).
source: Intriguingly, a cluster of Pou1f1 lineage progenitors (Pou1f1 Lin Prog) became distinguishable in the aggregate (control + damaged) neonatal AP analysis (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Cell proliferation genes and terms are enriched in Pou1f1 clusters in damaged versus control neonatal AP.
source: DEG and GO examination of the two Pou1f1 clusters together (Prolif Pou1f1+ cells and Pou1f1 Lin Prog) revealed enriched cell proliferation genes and terms in damaged versus control condition (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 2A; Figure 4—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Proliferative activity of PIT1+ cells increased upon damage in neonatal pituitary.
source: In accordance, in situ proliferative activity of the PIT1+ cells was found increased upon damage (Figure 4F), as well as of already GH-expressing cells (Figure 4F), the latter not observed in adult gland (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Proliferative activity of GH-expressing cells increased upon damage in neonatal pituitary, which was not observed in adult gland.
source: In accordance, in situ proliferative activity of the PIT1+ cells was found increased upon damage (Figure 4F), as well as of already GH-expressing cells (Figure 4F), the latter not observed in adult gland (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section, shown in Figure 4F, and supported by citation to Fu et al., 2012.

claim: There is an increase in SOX2+GH+ cells in damaged versus control neonatal gland.
source: Finally, there is also an increase in SOX2+GH+ cells in damaged versus control gland (Figure 4G), suggesting rising stem cell differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: NOTCH signaling is downregulated in the stem cells following injury in neonatal pituitary.
source: DEG and GO analysis of all SC clusters together revealed enriched NOTCH signaling terms in control versus damaged pituitary, or in others words, that NOTCH signaling is downregulated in the stem cells following the inflicted injury (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B; Figure 4—figure supplement 2—source data 2), which may be in line with the knowledge that NOTCH inhibition is needed for proper endocrine cell differentiation from stem/progenitor cells as observed during pituitary embryogenesis (Cox et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: NOTCH inhibition is needed for proper endocrine cell differentiation from stem/progenitor cells during pituitary embryogenesis.
source: DEG and GO analysis of all SC clusters together revealed enriched NOTCH signaling terms in control versus damaged pituitary, or in others words, that NOTCH signaling is downregulated in the stem cells following the inflicted injury (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B; Figure 4—figure supplement 2—source data 2), which may be in line with the knowledge that NOTCH inhibition is needed for proper endocrine cell differentiation from stem/progenitor cells as observed during pituitary embryogenesis (Cox et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to Cox et al., 2017 and Zhu et al., 2006.

claim: Restoration of the GH+ cell population in neonatal pituitary may encompass proliferative activation of PIT1+ progenitor and GH+ cell populations, and GH/somatotrope differentiation of SOX2+ stem cells.
source: Taken together, restoration of the GH+ cell population in the neonatal pituitary may encompass several mechanisms including proliferative activation of the PIT1+ (progenitor) and derived (or existing) GH+ cell populations, and GH/somatotrope differentiation of SOX2+ stem cells, together embodying the active nature of the neonatal gland.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on the regeneration data.

claim: The dynamic neonatal gland more efficiently regenerates after injury than the adult gland.
source: In conclusion, these data show that the dynamic neonatal gland more efficiently regenerates after injury than the adult gland, but that the already highly activated stem cell population does not show extra visible activation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on the regeneration experiments.

claim: The already highly activated stem cell population in neonatal pituitary does not show extra visible activation after injury.
source: In conclusion, these data show that the dynamic neonatal gland more efficiently regenerates after injury than the adult gland, but that the already highly activated stem cell population does not show extra visible activation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on the damage response data.

claim: The hybrid E/M phenotype of neonatal pituitary stem cells likely embodies their active participation in the intense maturation process of the neonatal gland.
source: Hence, the hybrid E/M phenotype of the neonatal pituitary stem cells likely embodies their active participation in the intense maturation process of the neonatal gland, as proposed during embryogenesis in human pituitary (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the discussion based on the observed hybrid E/M phenotype.

claim: Integrating neonatal mouse AP scRNA-seq dataset with fetal human pituitary data revealed considerable overlap.
source: Integrating our neonatal mouse AP scRNA-seq dataset with the recently published scRNA-seq data of fetal human pituitary (Zhang et al., 2020) revealed considerable overlap, including an analogous WNT landscape.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G.

claim: Early-postnatal (2-week-old) mouse pituitary stem cells show a paracrine-regulatory role, stimulating neighboring committed progenitor cells and stem cells to proliferate and expand.
source: A pronounced WNT profile has recently also been reported in the early-postnatal (2-week-old) mouse pituitary (Russell et al., 2021). Interestingly, this study showed a paracrine-regulatory role of these stem cells, stimulating neighboring committed progenitor cells (as well as stem cells) to proliferate and expand.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Russell et al., 2021.

claim: IL-6 is promptly upregulated in the adult pituitary, particularly in stem cells, following transgenically inflicted damage.
source: We recently found that IL-6 is promptly upregulated in the adult pituitary, in particular in its stem cells, following transgenically inflicted damage, associated with proliferative stem cell activation (Vennekens et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Vennekens et al., 2021.

claim: The pituitary reacts to damage differently according to developmental age.
source: Together, these findings suggest that the pituitary reacts to damage differently according to developmental age.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion in the discussion based on the observed differences between neonatal and adult damage response.

claim: Efficient regenerative capacity is present in other mouse organs at neonatal age (such as heart and cochlea), while seriously declining or disappearing in adulthood.
source: Interestingly, efficient regenerative capacity is also present in other mouse organs at neonatal age (such as heart and cochlea), while seriously declining or disappearing in adulthood (Cox et al., 2014; Lam and Sadek, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Cox et al., 2014 and Lam and Sadek, 2018.

claim: The JAK/STAT pathway may be the common denominator that lies at the basis of stem cell activation in the neonatal gland.
source: We provide support for the latter, and also propose that the JAK/STAT pathway may be the common denominator that lies at the basis of stem cell activation in the neonatal gland, hence also critical for organoid outgrowth (as we show with STATTIC and suggest with the Il6−/− mouse) and organoid expandability (as induced by the JAK/STAT-signaling factors IL-6, LIF, and IL-11).
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the discussion based on the cytokine and STATTIC experiments.
